units.summary: statusRecorder gains an optional onStatus callback field used to report the breaker outcome when the status is written. Unexported struct, but it drives breaker behavior.
units.headline: statusRecorder gets optional onStatus callback field
units.reason: Unexported field that does nothing until WriteHeader invokes it; the behavioral effect is reviewed in the WriteHeader and serveThroughBreaker units.

units.summary: WriteHeader now invokes onStatus with the final status as soon as it is recorded. This is what lets the breaker learn the outcome before the body ends.
units.headline: WriteHeader reports status to breaker callback immediately
units.reason: Calls a callback in the response write path that decides circuit breaker accounting, so timing of outcome reporting changes.
focus: callback runs synchronously inside WriteHeader, so it must not block or panic
repeated WriteHeader calls with code >= 200 invoke the callback again; only the sync.Once in the caller makes it once

units.summary: Adds a type alias groupBreaker for gobreaker's TwoStepCircuitBreaker so call sites share one breaker type. The alias is used across the router and the ST fallback.
units.headline: Add groupBreaker alias for two-step circuit breaker
units.reason: A type alias only; the behavior change comes from the constructor and serveThroughBreaker units.

units.summary: The per-group breaker constructor now builds a two-step breaker instead of a one-shot Execute breaker, with the same settings. All users, including the ST fallback, now get the two-step API.
units.headline: Group breakers are now gobreaker two-step breakers
units.reason: Changes the breaker implementation used in production for every group and ST destination.
focus: every caller of the returned breaker, including the ST fallback forward path, uses Allow and done correctly
IsExcluded settings still apply to errors passed to done

units.summary: The request now goes through cb.Allow and reports the outcome via done as soon as the response status is written, with a deferred fallback and panic handling guarded by sync.Once. This stops a streaming watch from holding the half-open trial slot.
units.headline: Breaker outcome reported at status write, not handler return
units.reason: Rewrites concurrency and error accounting for all proxied requests, with panic recovery and re-panic.
focus: every path after Allow succeeds calls done exactly once, including panic and http.ErrAbortHandler
status-time outcome uses the proxy failure already recorded by the error handler before WriteHeader
a 2xx watch that later fails mid-stream no longer counts against the backend
the 503 on Allow error is written through the traced writer

units.summary: Test helper signature switched to the groupBreaker alias to match production types.
units.headline: Test helper takes groupBreaker type
units.reason: Test-only type change that follows the production alias.

units.summary: The test now builds a two-step breaker to match the new production type. Assertions are unchanged.
units.headline: Half-open cap test uses two-step breaker
units.reason: Test-only constructor swap with no expectations changed.

units.summary: The helper trips the breaker via Allow and done with a forced failure instead of Execute. It silently does nothing if Allow errors.
units.headline: tripBreaker uses Allow/done instead of Execute
units.reason: Test-only helper adapted to the two-step API, same effect of one forced failure.
